proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article 12 gives Harpoon reversion rights but gives us no exit support, and Section 9.7 only offers a request-based return that Harpoon may satisfy by destruction on no fixed timetable. We added our fallback transition position: at least 90 days of assistance on any expiry or termination and return of our data within 30 days, carved out for data Harpoon retains rights to under the surviving reversion provisions.

ops.text: Transition Assistance; Return of AbbVie Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Harpoon shall (a) at AbbVie's request, provide AbbVie with reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following the effective date of such expiration or termination, and (b) notwithstanding the destruction election and timing in Section 9.7(a)-(b), within thirty (30) days after such effective date, return to AbbVie all data of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or control, other than data to which Harpoon retains rights under the surviving provisions of this Agreement, including Sections 12.6 and 12.7.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 12.11 requiring Harpoon, on any expiry or termination, to provide at least 90 days of transition assistance and to return AbbVie's data within 30 days, without disturbing Section 9.7's retention proviso or the Article 12 reversion regime.

quote: (a) as soon as reasonably practicable, destroy all copies of such Confidential Information in the possession of the other Party and confirm such destruction in writing to the requesting Party; or (b) as soon as reasonably practicable, deliver to the requesting Party, at such other Party's expense, all copies of such Confidential Information in the possession of such other Party
rationale: Article 12 contains detailed reversion mechanics running to Harpoon (Sections 12.6-12.7), a sell-off right (12.10.2) and survival provisions, but imposes no obligation on Harpoon to support AbbVie's wind-down or to return AbbVie's data on expiry or termination. The only return mechanic is Section 9.7, which is request-based, lets Harpoon elect destruction instead of delivery, and sets no deadline ("as soon as reasonably practicable"); Harpoon's other assistance obligations operate during the Term only. The rule therefore fails at the fallback. We insert a new Section 12.11 at the fallback level: at least 90 days of transition assistance available after any expiry or termination, and return of AbbVie data within 30 days of the effective date. The override is narrowed to the Section 9.7(a)-(b) destruction election and timing so Harpoon's one-copy retention proviso and back-up carve-out survive; limb (b) is confined to AbbVie data (not all AbbVie Confidential Information), uses lower-case "control" to avoid the IP-specific defined term, and carves out data Harpoon retains rights to under the surviving provisions, including Sections 12.6 and 12.7, so it does not collide with the reversion regime. We did not volunteer the preferred six-month period, then-current-rate charging, machine-readable format or deletion certification.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Harpoon shall ...", so both limbs are triggered by either event, and limb (a)'s request is made after that effective date rather than only in anticipation of expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) grants "reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days"; no six-month (or longer) period is stated. To reach preferred, change the period to "up to six (6) months".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: The insertion contains no pricing basis for the assistance; no "at Harpoon's then-current rates" language appears anywhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such effective date, return to AbbVie all data of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or control", with "such effective date" anchored to the expiration/termination date defined in limb (a), and the narrow override of Section 9.7(a)-(b) removes the destruction election and the "as soon as reasonably practicable" timing.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) specifies no format; add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to satisfy this element.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No post-return deletion or written certification obligation is inserted; retained Section 9.7(a) certification applies only to the destruction election that limb (b) overrides, and only on request.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" governs both limbs (a) and (b); the trigger is not confined to anticipated expiry or to a particular termination ground.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): Harpoon shall "at AbbVie's request, provide AbbVie with reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following the effective date of such expiration or termination" — the floor is expressly "at least" 90 days and runs post-termination.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of "all data of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or control" within 30 days of the effective date, overriding Section 9.7's destruction election and open-ended timing; the carve-out is limited to data Harpoon retains rights to under surviving provisions (Sections 12.6-12.7), i.e. the reversion package, not AbbVie's own data generally.

verification.notes: Position-complete at the fallback: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (90-day floor of post-termination assistance and 30-day data return), so the redline is acceptable as drafted even though four preferred elements (six months, then-current rates, machine-readable format, deletion certification) were deliberately not volunteered. Minimality holds: the insertion is a single concise paragraph tracking the fallback checklist only; it adds no survival tail, no at-own-expense term, no damages or procedural extras, and does not import the preferred six-month/rate/format/certification mechanics. The "notwithstanding the destruction election and timing in Section 9.7(a)-(b)" override is narrowly targeted rather than a blanket override of Section 9.7, and is necessary because the retained sentence would otherwise let Harpoon satisfy return by destruction "as soon as reasonably practicable" — i.e. it cures a contradictory retained sentence rather than adding scope. Intent preserved: Harpoon's one-copy retention proviso and automatic back-up carve-out in Section 9.7(b), the Section 12.10.2 sell-off right, and the Article 12 reversion regime (Sections 12.6-12.7) all survive, and limb (b) is expressly carved out for data Harpoon retains rights to under surviving provisions, so no dangling cross-reference or collision is created. Residual drafting point for the drafter (not a failure): the rendered insertion carries only the heading "Transition Assistance; Return of AbbVie Data." without the Section 12.11 number referenced in the rationale — number the clause on execution so cross-references to Article 12 remain coherent. If pressed toward the preferred position, the minimum operative repairs are: extend limb (a) to "up to six (6) months at Harpoon's then-current rates", add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to limb (b), and add a limb (c) requiring deletion of AbbVie data after return with written certification.
